The researchers used SolidWorks 2021 to design a virtual 3D model of a wind turbine.
They generated a total of 642 synthetic images with variations in background, camera angle, and lighting effects for the four defect types.
The U-Net deep learning model was trained using the Adam optimizer and Dice Loss function.
The trained U-Net model achieved a Dice Coefficient of 0.658 on the test data.
The researchers used the Unity game engine and its Perception Package to generate the synthetic images and corresponding semantic segmentation ground truth.
Wind turbines provided almost 8.4% of the total generated electricity in the United States in 2020.
There are more than 700,800 wind turbines running across 44 states in the United States.
Blade cracks, leading edge erosion, delamination, and lightning strike damage are four common types of wind turbine blade defects.
Blade cracks can lead to eventual failure of the turbine if not identified in the initial stages.
Leading edge erosion can reduce the efficiency of power generation over time.
Delamination of wind turbine blades is caused by extreme weather, humidity, or mechanical stresses.
Lightning strike damage can affect the generator, control systems, power electronics, or blades of a wind turbine.
Detecting blade defects early is critical for ensuring uninterrupted power generation and avoiding catastrophic failures.
Traditional manual inspection methods for wind turbine blades are time-consuming and expensive.
The researchers used the Dice Coefficient as the loss function during model training and as the evaluation metric for the test set.
